packs.title: Harbor, houses and the wider city
packs.promise: Join actual tours, galleries, a screening and coastal visits across Salem.

q.s: Visit PEM, then propose an original pairing from what you encountered.
st: Explore open galleries with a valid admission ticket and give the visit time beyond the first room.
Choose two works or objects that seem to disagree or unexpectedly belong together. Read their available interpretation without copying it.
After looking, write a short original proposal for placing them in conversation: the shared question, one difference and a title of your own.

q.s: Walk the open wharf and reconstruct one practical movement through it.
st: Walk the permitted wharf route, keeping clear of work areas and water edges.
Select one practical movement to trace on paper, such as a person carrying a load from land toward the water. Use three features you can actually see to support your route.
Explain which parts are observed and which are your own reconstruction. If NPS interpretation gives a different account, preserve that distinction.

q.s: Give the Willows a quiet interval without needing its seasonal businesses.
st: Choose an open public spot where you can stop without blocking anyone or approaching a water edge.
Spend ten quiet minutes noticing changes in wind, sound or movement. Let the interval run without photographing other people.
Afterward, describe one change you would have missed by passing straight through. You do not need to report a particular feeling.

packs.title: Essex Street to the waterfront in two afternoons
packs.promise: Connect historic interiors, a garden, public books and local art through short downtown walks.

q.s: Explore Ropes Garden, then invent a tiny garden using a principle you noticed.
st: Walk the open garden paths and notice how a route, an edge or a planted area shapes your movement.
Choose one useful principle, such as making a pause or separating spaces. Describe the actual feature that suggested it.
Invent a small garden for a doorstep, balcony or imagined patch of ground. Sketch or describe an original arrangement using that principle rather than copying this garden.

q.s: Walk a bounded stretch out and back, letting its layout set the pace.
st: Walk the open sidewalk from the Phillips House block toward Cambridge Street, crossing only where permitted.
Choose a comfortable place to pause. Notice how the spacing of entrances, trees or setbacks affects a pedestrian’s route; do not inspect private interiors.
Return along the public route. Describe one detail that appeared differently on the return and why its position mattered.

q.s: Browse the independent bookshop and choose a path through unfamiliar reading.
st: Browse the books available during public shop hours without blocking the shelves.
Choose one available book outside your usual subject or genre, and look at its permitted summary or contents without copying passages.
Choose a second available book that could take that curiosity in another direction. Write your own brief reason for the pairing; you need not buy either.
